$comment: P2.8: agreement types and template catalogue, as a default for Facilities Management.
THIS IS A STARTING POINT, NOT A DECISION. No client has reviewed it. It exists so Phase 1 can
be built against something concrete rather than waiting, and so the conversation with a client
is 'change these' rather than 'what do you need', which is a much easier conversation to have.
Every row is tenant-editable configuration (P0-D4). Nothing here is compiled into the product:
a tenant that needs a fifteenth agreement type adds one, and a tenant that never uses framework
riskLevel drives the low-touch path: a low-risk type is one of its four preconditions
(blueprint 6.2). It is deliberately conservative here: the cost of routing a simple NDA through
review is an hour of somebody's time, and the cost of auto-approving a TFM contract is a
FAMILY groups the fourteen types into the five kinds of paper an FM team actually handles:
framework and master agreements, service delivery contracts, project and supply work, legal
and compliance instruments, and lifecycle documents that amend or end something else.
It exists because the type name answers 'what is this contract about' and not 'what kind of
document am I holding', and a person triaging a queue needs the second question answered
first. An NDA and a five-year TFM agreement are both 'contracts' and nothing else about them

agreementTypes.name: Master Services Agreement
agreementTypes.why: The umbrella every call-off hangs from. Its liability and indemnity terms govern work nobody has scoped yet, which is what makes it the highest-risk document in the estate.

agreementTypes.name: Total Facilities Management Agreement
agreementTypes.why: One supplier takes the whole estate. Highest value, longest term, and the hardest to exit: a failed TFM contract is an operational emergency, not a procurement problem.

agreementTypes.name: Hard FM Services Agreement
agreementTypes.why: Mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire and lifts. Statutory compliance sits here: a lapse in fire or lift inspection is a criminal liability for the client, not just a service failure.

agreementTypes.name: Soft FM Services Agreement
agreementTypes.why: Cleaning, catering, security, waste, grounds. Lower statutory exposure than hard FM, but the largest headcount, which is why TUPE almost always applies.

agreementTypes.name: Planned Preventive Maintenance Agreement
agreementTypes.why: Scheduled maintenance to a written regime. Medium rather than low because the schedule is the compliance evidence: if the regime is wrong, every visit against it is wrong.

agreementTypes.name: Reactive Maintenance Call-Off
agreementTypes.why: Called off against agreed rates when something breaks. The risk is not the individual job, it is that unpriced work accumulates past any approval threshold one call-off at a time.

agreementTypes.name: Framework Agreement
agreementTypes.why: Several suppliers, no committed volume. High because it sets the terms for everything called off under it, often for years, and is frequently signed before anyone knows what will be bought.

agreementTypes.name: Statement of Work
agreementTypes.why: Scoped work under an existing MSA. Low only because the MSA already carries the liability and indemnity terms: a SOW with no parent agreement is not low risk and must not use this type.

agreementTypes.name: Equipment Supply and Installation
agreementTypes.why: Plant and equipment with installation. Title, warranty and defects liability matter more here than service levels, and the warranty usually outlives the installer's involvement.

agreementTypes.name: Consultancy and Professional Services
agreementTypes.why: Advice rather than labour: surveys, design, compliance audits. The exposure is professional indemnity and who owns the deliverable, not service credits.

agreementTypes.name: Non-Disclosure Agreement
agreementTypes.why: Signed before anything else, usually in volume, usually on our paper. The genuine low-touch case: standard wording, no value, no service obligation.

agreementTypes.name: Data Processing Agreement
agreementTypes.why: Where a supplier processes personal data: access control, CCTV, visitor management, occupancy analytics. High because the terms are largely non-negotiable in law and getting them wrong is a regulatory exposure rather than a commercial one.

agreementTypes.name: Variation Agreement
agreementTypes.why: Amends an existing contract. The risk is not the change but the drift: a chain of small variations can move a contract a long way from what was approved, and each one looks small.

agreementTypes.name: Termination and Settlement Agreement
agreementTypes.why: Ends a relationship and settles what is owed. High because it is usually drafted under pressure, waives rights permanently, and is the document most likely to be read by a court.
